lines.text: Many learners say: Can you give me an advice?
Better: Can you give me some advice?
We can't count advice. Say some.
Some! Can you give me some advice?

data.wrong: Can you give me an advice?
data.right: Can you give me some advice?
data.why: We can't count advice. Say some.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia, saran bisa dihitung: “dua saran”. Di bahasa Inggris, advice tidak bisa dihitung, jadi pakai some, bukan an.
native.caption: Pernah bilang begini? “Can you give me an advice?” 😅 Advice tidak bisa dihitung, jadi pakai some: “Can you give me some advice?” Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “some”. Ucapkan dengan lantang: “Can you give me some advice?” lalu tulis satu saran untuk temanmu. Latihan gratis lainnya di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian, “saran” can be counted: “dua saran”. In English, advice cannot be counted, so use some, not an.
en.caption: Ever say this? “Can you give me an advice?” 😅 Advice cannot be counted, so use some: “Can you give me some advice?” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
